title: Adaptive prompt spine: cross-request microcache & slab coordination
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: Current KV-prefix caching reuses fragments across requests but leaves a gap for small, high-frequency prompt overlaps (e.g., onboarding flows, short system prompts). These cause repeated KV population churn and scattered GPU slab allocation which increases DRAM/GPU fragmentation and tail latency during microbursts.

Goal: Implement an adaptive microcache layer and a slab-collation coordinator that (1) canonicalizes and fingerprints short prompt 'spines' across requests, (2) opportunistically co-locates frequently re-used fragments into contiguous GPU slabs, and (3) provides a light-weight admission and eviction credit system that plays well with continuous batching to reduce duplicate KV population and improve GPU memory packing.

Scope & constraints:
- Must be compatible with existing KV store API and GPU-residency semantics (no protocol changes to customer-facing APIs).
- Low CPU overhead for fingerprinting; prefer SIMD-friendly hashes and bloom prefilters.
- Prefer incremental rollout (canary customers) and safe fallback to existing prefix cache on mismatch or memory pressure.
- Maintain deterministic eviction debugging for post-mortems (logs + stable heuristics).

Design approach:
1) Prompt spine fingerprinting: define a compact canonicalization (strip non-essential whitespace, normalize templated slots, limit to first N tokens for short prompts) and compute 64-bit spine fingerprints. Store spine -> fragment list mappings in the microcache index.
2) Microcache admission: a tiny LRU bloom-backed in-memory microcache per-GPU node (capacity: ~1-2% of full KV entries) that keeps hot spine mappings and fast path for KV lookups during batching. This reduces the need for full KV (shard) lookups for short repeated spines.
3) Slab collation coordinator: when the microcache detects repeated co-access patterns for fragments across spines, emit a slab-collation hint to the allocator. Allocator will try to place those fragments contiguously on the same GPU slab/slot pool to improve locality and reduce fragmentation. Collation hints are best-effort and subject to slab pressure policies.
4) Eviction crediting: assign temporal credits for collated fragments; on eviction decisions, prefer removing un-collated or low-credit entries. Credits decay over time and are topped up on cache hits. This aligns slab residency with real reuse.
5) Cross-request dedupe algorithm: use a two-stage de-dup path during continuous batching: (a) microcache bloom filter and fingerprint match to short-circuit duplicate fragment decode, (b) content-aware equality check (cheap length/hash) before using existing KV entry. Avoid heavy LSH similarity in the fast path; use it as a background consolidation job.
6) Background consolidation: periodic job that runs LSH/simhash clustering on longer-lived fragments to detect near-duplicates and emit canonicalization actions (merge or redirect fragment IDs to canonical entries) during low-load windows.

Success metrics (target):
- 15-30% reduction in GPU-resident KV entries for targeted workloads (chatbots with repeated short system prompts).
- 10-20% reduction in P95 token latency under microburst traffic.
- 10-25% reduction in GPU memory fragmentation measured by internal slab utilization metric.
- No regression (>1%) in throughput for large-context generation workloads.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: Unit/integration tests and offline simulation using recent production traces (simulate 30d of requests).
- Phase 1 (internal canary): enable microcache without slab collation on 5% serving capacity; collect metrics for two weeks.
- Phase 2 (collation on for low-traffic nodes): enable slab collation hints with conservative slab thresholds on 1-2 nodes; enable logging for eviction decisions.
- Phase 3: wider rollout with gradual decrease of collation thresholds if metrics look good; enable background consolidation job during off-peak windows.

Testing & telemetry:
- New telemetry: spine-hit-rate, microcache-short-circuits, collation-hit-rate, eviction-credit-distribution, slab-compactness index.
- Bench harness: reproduce baseline with continuous-batching emulation and measure tail latency under synthetic microburst traffic.
- A/B dashboard: compare canary vs. baseline for latency, GPU resident count, and cost-per-token.

Open tradeoffs / unresolved decisions:
- Canonicalization aggressiveness: how much to normalize (slot masking) vs. risk of false dedupe. Proposed conservative defaults and a 'normalize-level' config per customer.
- Microcache sizing: we propose 1-2% of full KV entries as starting point; may tune by workload.
- Whether slab-collation hints should be global (coordinator) or local heuristic; currently implementing a hybrid where microcache emits hints and local allocator respects them when safe.

Deliverables:
- RFC + simulation results -> runtime-1.22 feature flag.
- Implementation of microcache index, admission policy, and short-circuit path.
- Slab collation hint API and allocator integration.
- Background consolidation job and offline tooling.

Success criteria for GA: sustained improvements on target metrics for at least two customer cohorts and absence of correctness incidents (no observable content regressions).

2026-03-10 Design review: agreed on conservative default for normalize-level=1 (strip whitespace + canonical slot tokens up to first 32 tokens). Emma approved per-tenant opt-out flag (opt_out_prompt_spine_dedupe).
